summary: Otho Holland Lloyd, Constance Wilde's brother, and his wife Nellie. Wilde calls them jointly 'the important uncle and aunt of our son and heir'.
certainty_reasoning: MARRIED: Wilde addresses them as a couple in the same breath - 'you and Otho, the important uncle and aunt of our son and heir' - and asks after 'little Otho', their son, in a later letter to Otho alone. NO DATES: the marriage year is not given on any page read here and is not inferred, so the edge carries no start or end.

sources.quote: I will let you and Otho, the important uncle and aunt of our son and heir, know how she gets on. I hope you will get through your own confinement as easily as Constance - I am sure you will.
sources.context: Wilde to Nellie Lloyd, [postmark 5 June 1885], 16 Tite Street (MS Holland). Quoted for the pairing: the two of them named together as uncle and aunt, and Nellie's own pregnancy in the next sentence.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: That they were a married couple, and both expecting.
